translations.text: Of Shenoute.

During the night when we disciplined these ignorant people in the house of God, toward dawn on the [?] day of the month of Tybi, they were crowded together and bound while we questioned those impure strangers in Christ’s place.
I considered this matter as I appealed to the Lord of all: whether it was right to leave them in these congregations, or whether their root should be torn out of them.

Look, a man assuming the appearance of authority, sent by someone greater than himself, pushed his way through the doors of those places without asking. Another followed him, as though he too were subordinate to this one.
He seized me as I was passing through the courtyards of these places, distressed over those pestilent men.
He began to raise his hand against me and fight with me, acting as though he cared about those people.
I resisted him in turn, so as to seize him by the object fastened to his neck or around his throat, saying these words: “I am not afraid at all, nor am I troubled about who you are.
What is the matter with you? Why do you hide yourself instead of revealing yourself?
“If you are a spirit or an angel who has come from God, I too am his servant. And even if you stay, I will not stay. Or tell me whether you were sent [?].
“Was it they who sinned against God, or was it we who sinned against him because we intend to remove them from our midst? No, we will not let you go; rather, I will fight against you even more.”
While I was saying these things and others, he struggled with me, wanting to leave. I struggled with him and gained strength against him and over him.
And when he acted like someone who wanted to throw me down, I struck him down on the ground instead.
I held his chest down with my feet while standing and calling to the brothers whom I could see around me, supporting me throughout this struggle: “Grab this other one!”

For I was thinking to myself, “It is impossible for a human being to overcome a spirit or an angel of God. Rather, people fall to the ground in fear when they see them, and those who have appeared to them can barely steady them in this state of mind.”
And look, those two quickly revealed themselves to be demons. And I understood that this is Satan’s effort to deceive the crowds gathered together
in places, making them tolerate the secret, ungodly practices of those who do scandalous deeds among them, until the weeds far outnumber the good seed.
For people have chosen to please those counted among the evildoers rather than to please God.

This is how it is: one person was not expelled because of his father, because they were ashamed before him; another because of his brother; another because of an empty desire; another because of hypocrisy and favoritism, with others showing them consideration—
those who defile and befoul everything for people’s sake and not for Jesus’ sake, as we have said many times in many places—not we alone, but also those before us who were truly God’s chosen ones.
Then shall we find testimony in other forms concerning cutting off from the body the limbs that have rotted in it?
Are the Scriptures not sufficient, commanding us to uproot and tear down, to build and plant?
But I have told you, brothers, that the enemy deceives many of those who readily believe every word and every spirit.
This is what happens in many places: many fight on behalf of ungodliness because they give their attention to deceitful spirits and the teachings of demons.
Indeed, it is not wrong for someone who loves Christ to fight with a good spirit if it appears to him.
The spirit itself loves him all the more and rejoices over him.

For it knows that he is not opposing it, but is keeping watch and guarding himself against bowing down to a demon and coming under the authority of a [?] spirit while thinking that it is a holy angel.
Only, even if I live in the same places with people—men and women, grown men and grown women, little boys and little girls—
Whether I receive the sacrament with them or they receive it with me, whether I pray with them or they pray with me, whether I eat bread with them and they eat with me, or my hand and
[?] their hands in this one cup at this one table, and dare to destroy God’s creatures through any impurity or defilement in this house, or these houses and these places [?]

built in his name with great labor and large amounts of gold, bronze, and every kind of material—you will not be able to count them all until we have completed them—so that souls may benefit and souls may go before God in complete purity.
not only am I their enemy throughout the days of my life, as they have said many times;

Even if I speak to them with peaceful words, even if I act like someone who rejoices with them or blesses them, they are all the more accursed, along with all their deeds. And those who know about their deeds and cover them up are all the more accursed with them, along with all their deeds.
